title: Session Management
description: Implement secure session management including cookie configuration, session fixation prevention, and proper expiration strategies.

data.text: **Session management** tracks authenticated users across requests. While JWT is popular, server-side sessions remain the most secure option for many applications because the sensitive data never leaves the server.

cards.title: Server-Side Session
cards.description: Session ID stored in cookie, data stored server-side
cons: Scales with sticky sessions or shared store

data.text: Cookies are the most common transport for session IDs. Misconfigured cookies are a frequent source of vulnerabilities. Every cookie must be hardened against interception and tampering.

data.title: Secure Cookie Policy (C#)
data.content: Configuring secure session cookies in ASP.NET Core

data.title: HttpOnly Cookies
data.text: Always set HttpOnly on authentication cookies. This prevents JavaScript (including XSS payloads) from reading the cookie value.

**Session fixation** occurs when an attacker sets a victim's session ID before login, then waits for the victim to authenticate with that known ID. After login, the attacker uses the same session ID to hijack the session.

items: Attacker visits site and receives session ID `S123`
Attacker tricks victim into clicking a link that sets `S123`
Server upgrades `S123` to an authenticated session
Attacker uses `S123` to access victim's account

data.title: Prevention
data.text: Always regenerate the session ID after authentication. ASP.NET Core does this automatically when signing in, but verify if you implement custom session stores.

items: **Absolute expiration**: Session expires after a fixed time (e.g., 8 hours)
**Sliding expiration**: Session is extended with activity up to a max (e.g., 30 min idle, 8 hours max)
**Hard logout on role change**: Invalidate session if user permissions change

data.title: Sliding Expiration with Redis
data.content: Storing session state in Redis with automatic expiration

data.text: Limit the number of concurrent sessions per user. If a user logs in from a new device, invalidate older sessions. This prevents credential sharing and limits the blast radius of a stolen session cookie.

items.text: Set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite on all auth cookies
items.hint: SameSite=Lax blocks most CSRF while preserving UX

items.text: Use absolute and sliding expiration together
items.hint: Sliding alone can keep sessions alive indefinitely

items.text: Store session data server-side with a short TTL

items.hint: e.g., max 3 active sessions per user

items.text: Invalidate sessions on password change or role change

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use HttpOnly and Secure cookies
data.takeaway: Proper session management prevents hijacking and limits the damage from stolen credentials.
